Use case: historical-scene. Create ONE photorealistic architectural environment image for a coherent Dream of the Red Chamber / Grand View Garden reference collection, intended as a later 3D modeling reference, not a modeled asset or a technical blueprint. Landscape 3:2 frame, highest available native detail, no collage. The user's provided garden image is a STYLE reference: borrow its credible stone, timber and tiles, sophisticated layered gardens, convincing reflections and exceptional natural light, not its exact buildings. This is a literary aristocratic private garden in a premodern Chinese setting, with Jiangnan craftsmanship; do not falsely date the novel to one precise dynasty. Give the image a captivating, specific spatial idea rather than generic television-period scenery. Deep focus and restrained architectural perspective, clear load-bearing columns, plausible eaves, contiguous paths and roof junctions, real material scale, visible bases and thresholds, keep key structures legible through planting. Finely textured lime plaster, grey clay tiles, naturally finished hardwood and worked limestone, restrained jade, warm parchment and botanical color. No people, modern objects, electric lights, impossible floating buildings, plastic CGI, anime, oversaturated red, endless identical red lanterns, Forbidden City composition, gratuitous golden roofs, captions, logos, watermark or readable signage.

Asset: 蘅芜苑·石骨幽芳
Hengwuyuan, Xue Baochai's exceptionally restrained courtyard. Chapter 17 anchors: tall exquisite perforated limestone scholar-rock mass screens the entrance and partly conceals the residence; a five-bay clean main house with a rolled ridge / barrel-curved roof canopy and covered verandas on four sides; green-tinted wooden windows and smoothly finished walls. The court contains NO flowering trees: no magnolia, cherry, peach or flowering shrub beds. Its beauty comes from strange fragrant low herbs, narrow-leaved grasses and fine creeping vines threading the rock holes, falling over ledges and lightly winding near steps. A three-quarter slightly elevated oblique view from beside the rock screen so the five-bay hall and circulation remain intelligible; limestone is weathered porous karst, not a pile of random boulders. Through one open window a nearly bare pale room, a plain earthenware vase with a few chrysanthemums, two books and tea utensils, muted blue gauze. After-rain overcast light with a soft cool shaft, silver limestone, desaturated pale olive and subtle amber timber; quietly arresting through sculptural negative space, no generic lush floral fantasy.
